investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-31T00:55–01:03Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the createAgent call.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0/6 nodes available for scheduling. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns a VM identity, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256) receives no evidence at all. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Lower probability — a transient spike in concurrent remote-agent demand (e.g., multiple eval runs or user workloads) temporarily exhausted the pool; capacity may self-recover once existing pods terminate.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the snapshot URL returns a freshly generated artifact (snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300) when fetched at the time of investigation, it would indicate the eval captured a transient window between workflow runs and the problem has self-resolved.

If GitHub Actions run history shows the snapshot-publishing workflow completed successfully within the past 300 minutes and the published artifact is still stale, a GitHub Pages CDN caching or propagation issue would become the more likely cause.

If the workflow run history shows the workflow fired on schedule and succeeded but the snapshot age is still reported as 719 minutes, a bug in the snapshotAgeMinutes calculation logic in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) or in the snapshot's own generatedAt field would need to be investigated.
If all sibling checks had also failed, a shared infrastructure failure (DNS, CDN, GitHub Pages outage) would be a stronger candidate than a workflow scheduling gap.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks the GitHub Actions workflow run recency for the snapshot-publishing workflow — asserting that the last successful run completed within the past 250 minutes — to catch scheduling gaps before the snapshot staleness contract is violated.

Add an eval that detects the staleAfterMinutes vs maxAgeMinutes discrepancy between infra/evals/status/features.json and infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json, asserting that the registry staleAfterMinutes value is always less than or equal to the contract maxAgeMinutes value for the same check.

Add a trend eval that tracks snapshotAgeMinutes over consecutive runs and alerts when the value is increasing monotonically across multiple runs, indicating the workflow has stopped publishing rather than waiting for a single threshold breach.

evidenceDigest.message: Published observability snapshot is missing live workflow data or is stale; Expected evidence assertion failed: snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 719
